label: L=9 copy phase, outputting 3rd token (input = 2nd original token), sparse
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely in length-9 sequences (98.9% of mass) at t=11, i.e. recall_idx=2, where the input is the fed-back 2nd original token and the output is the 3rd (80% of mass); weaker spillover at recall_idx 1 and 3 (and a few at the last step). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, nor on L<=7. Within that context it is very sparse (~2% of L=9 recall_idx=2 steps): it is strongly enriched when the input token is f, b or d (also digits 0/2), and when the output is i, j, c or u; the top activations are almost all inputs f/b. Restricting to inputs f/b/d raises precision to ~11% but loses half the mass, so the token-level selectivity is not captured by a simple rule. Low activation magnitude overall (max 0.004).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=b (+3.44), phase=2 & in_tok=d (+3.24), phase=2 & in_tok=f (+2.96), orig4=c (+2.32), orig3=i (+2.03), t=10 (+1.91). Lower it: orig8=- (-2.96), orig7=- (-1.92), orig4=p (-1.76), to_go=2 (-1.69).
